description_en: Located upstream from Sīrasthān (DLK0120), on the right bank of the Nabhi River and 800 meters from its confluence with the Chhamghate, the site of Nābhisthān includes two still-active flame temple, the "main flame" (baḍijvālā,DLK0150) and "Indra's flame".The temple is part of an area know as Pañcakośī. The sites of the Pañcakośī are visited by pilgrims from all over western Nepal. The sites are notorious for their flame temples (natural gas flames), said to mark places where Satī's body parts fell while Śiva carried her charred body (Lecomte-Tilouine 2009). Nābhisthān is the place where Satī's navel (nābhi) fell.The temple is built on the model of Newar temples with multiple roofs and a peristyle. It is built with bricks and mud mortar. The temple's door faces south. The stone door frames are older than the brick structure. They are decorated with bas-reliefs of volutes. A bas-relief of a rosette decorates the door lintel. Inside the sanctum, the natural flame is housed in a small niche on the west wall, right after the door.The door jambs can be dated from c. 12th-15th century. The brick structure of the temple is more recent, potentially from the 19th century. The monument is briefly mentioned inSharma 2012, p. 70 andAndolfatto 2019, p. 172-173.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
